title: Renewal Gradualization & Usage-Slope Trigger Framework
creator: Asha Patel
description: Proposal for a ruleset and orchestration playbook that replaces a single-step annual true-up with a phased renewal uplift tied to a customer's recent usage trajectory (usage slope). Goals: reduce sticker shock on renewals, improve expansion capture for rapid adopters, and limit revenue leakage while keeping contracts simple for sales and legal.
comments: 2026-03-02 — Asha: Initial draft submitted. Key assumption: usage slope (3-month linear fit) is predictive of next-12-month consumption for >60% of enterprise customers. Need modeling from Finance and Billing to validate assumptions.

2026-03-04 — Finance (Maya Lin): Ran cohort sims on 420 enterprise accounts. Results: phased 3-step uplift captures 86% of near-term expansion versus 100% lump-sum true-up, while reducing average renewal churn risk by ~1.9 percentage points.

2026-03-05 — Legal (Carlos Rivera): Draft language for staggered uplift clause reviewed. Requested explicit cutoff windows and a cap on cumulative uplift per year. Also asked to flag any state-specific consumer protection rules for deferred overage billing.

2026-03-06 — Sales Ops (Priya Singh): Concern about quota crediting if revenue comes phased; proposed a standardized booking guidance doc and sample invoice language to send to customers during renewal negotiations.

2026-03-07 — Engineering (Ravi Menon): ENG impact: minimal billing pipeline changes for deferral metadata, but require a new flag on contract objects and a job to apply phased adjustments. Estimated 2 sprints in billing team.

2026-03-08 — PM Review (Asha): Consolidated feedback. Decided to pilot with mid-market cohort first (contracts <$150k ARR) and selected 3-month phased cadence: 40% at renewal, 30% at 90 days, 30% at 180 days with a reconciliation true-up at month 12 if overage beyond forecast persists.

2026-03-09 — Data (Noah Kim): Added two observational checks: (1) ensure lookback window excludes onboarding spikes (use baseline-exclusion rule), (2) require minimum 3 months of production usage to be eligible for slope-triggered phased uplift.

2026-03-10 — PM (Asha): Submitted playbook to Review board and attached sample customer comms and contract amendment language. Awaiting legal sign-off and billing implementation estimation confirmation.

2026-03-10 — Reviewer (Elena Foster, Head of Renewals): Asked for a rollback guardrail: if customer disputes uplift within 30 days, auto-hold second/third tranche pending manual review. Engineering to add hold flag to billing pipeline.
2026-03-10 — Sales (Jamal Edwards): Requested an optional accelerator discount for 3‑year deals when customers accept upfront full uplift (to keep option for larger multi-year commitments).
decisions: Phased cadence chosen: 40% at renewal, 30% at 90d, 30% at 180d, with annual reconciliation
Eligibility: >= 3 months of steady production usage, usage-slope positive over 3 months and not an onboarding spike
Cap: cumulative uplift capped at 45% of current ARR inside a 12-month window (legal request)
Sales accelerator: optional 3-year upfront full-uplift discount (negotiated on deal-by-deal basis)
next_steps: Legal to finalize amendment language and state-specific billing constraints — due 2026-03-18 (owner: Carlos)
Billing/Engineering to provide implementation plan and sprint estimates including hold-flag and tranche invoicing — due 2026-03-17 (owner: Ravi)
Data to produce final cohort simulation with sensitivity bands and expected ARR capture vs. churn delta — due 2026-03-14 (owner: Noah)
GT M (Sales Enablement) to produce one-pager, sample customer email, and contract playbook for AE usage — due 2026-03-20 (owner: Priya)
Run a legal + finance tabletop with 3 sample accounts before pilot launch — schedule week of 2026-03-22
acceptance_criteria: Legal sign-off on amendment language and uplift cap
Billing implementation completed in sandbox with hold-flag and tranche invoicing tested
Data simulation confirms >=75% of revenue that a lump-sum true-up would capture while showing reduced renewal churn risk in pilot cohort
Sales enablement materials produced and AEs briefed
Pilot launch checklist completed and pilot cohort roster approved by Head of Renewals
risks: Customers perceive phased billing as complexity and may request full upfront payment — mitigated via clear comms and optional accelerator discount
Billing pipeline changes may introduce accounting complexity for revenue recognition — mitigate by involving Accounting/RevRec early
Edge cases where usage spikes are driven by short-term seasonality could trigger inappropriate uplifts; data rules must exclude onboarding/seasonal spikes
Legal or state billing regulations may limit deferred invoicing in certain territories — require territory gating and manual review for affected customers
